 Sweeping sunscreen testing reforms announced by the TGA
 In the wake of CHOICE's sunscreen testing last year, the way sunscreens are tested is about to change. by Mark Serrels Last updated: 27 Oct 2026 
 Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook 
 Share on X (Opens in new window) X 
 Share on LinkedIn (Opens in new window) LinkedIn 
 Share on Telegram (Opens in new window) Telegram 
 As first reported by the ABC , the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) has announced a new set of changes to the way sunscreens are tested in Australia.
These changes come in the wake of CHOICE’s sunscreen testing in June 2025 , which revealed that 16 out of 20 sunscreens failed to meet their SPF claims . Now, after a period of public consultation the TGA is taking action, proposing a new set of stricter rules around SPF testing, many of which will be introduced in the very near future.
 Under these new rules, brands will be forced to test sunscreens multiple times and send the results to the TGA before going to market. Crucially, brands also have to test the finished product as opposed to the base formula, and continue testing sunscreens throughout their shelf life.
 CHOICE welcomes TGA announcement
 Andy Kelly, CHOICE director of consumer impact, welcomed the changes.
“CHOICE welcomes the TGA’s proposed sunscreen reforms, following CHOICE testing last year which found 16 of 20 sunscreen products did not live up to their SPF claims – revealing an urgent need for changes to the way sunscreen is regulated.” 
 CHOICE welcomes the TGA’s proposed sunscreen reforms, following CHOICE testing last year which found 16 of 20 sunscreen products did not live up to their SPF claims
 Andy Kelly, CHOICE Director of Consumer Impact 
 “We’re pleased to see the TGA has proposed stricter rules which would require sunscreen brands to test their finished product, rather than just the base formula, and provide the results to the TGA before the product is listed. 
 “Brands would also be required to continuously test their products following listing. Currently, sunscreen brands are not required to provide any SPF testing data to the TGA unless requested, so this change would greatly improve the transparency around how brands have tested their products.
 “However, the TGA is not proposing to routinely monitor and evaluate test results. Sunscreen brands would also only be required to provide test results confidentially to the TGA. 
 “In the interest of transparency and public safety, we believe these results should be made available to everyone and that the TGA should routinely monitor test results, as well as conduct its own compliance testing program,” says Kelly. 
 Read more:
 We tested the SPF claims of 20 sunscreens. 16 failed 
 Strengthening accreditation rules for labs
 After an ABC report discovered many of the sunscreens that failed CHOICE testing were using an overseas lab , the TGA is also hoping to strengthen accreditation rules for the labs that undertake sunscreen tests.
 “CHOICE also supports the TGA’s recommended changes to how labs conducting SPF testing are regulated, following concerns around the reliability of some laboratories,” said Kelly. 
“Under the proposed reforms, any labs conducting SPF testing for products available in Australia would require international accreditation.” 
 “In a country where around two in three people will be diagnosed with skin cancer in their lifetime, consumers deserve to trust the claims on sunscreen products are accurate. These proposed reforms are an important step towards ensuring this is the case. We look forward to continuing to work with the TGA to improve the regulation of sunscreens in Australia.”

 In the past year alone we've uncovered systemic issues with sunscreens , investigated shonky supermarket pricing , fought for stronger scam protections and helped make complex energy pricing fairer and clearer .
 CHOICE is here to provide unbiased advice and independent testing in our world-class labs. We buy the products we test, just like you do, and our expert reviews are influence free . We’re here to help you choose smarter. Hopefully you’ll also save some money along the way.
Thanks to CHOICE, you’ll never be alone when a business treats you unfairly. You can support our work by joining or donating to our cause.
